pick.headline: Noriega takes refuge in the Vatican's embassy in Panama
pick.summary: On December 24, 1989, General Manuel Noriega, hunted by US forces, took refuge in the Vatican's nunciature in Panama City.
pick.significance: US troops surrounded the building and blared loud music at it; Noriega surrendered on January 3, 1990.
pick.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of December 26, 1989, carried Madrid EFE on Cuba's Alarcon saying Noriega would have been granted asylum, as his refuge in the nunciature was confirmed, and Havana radio protesting the US siege of Cuba's embassy.

alternates.headline: GIA hijacks Air France flight 8969 in Algiers
alternates.summary: On December 24, 1994, gunmen of Algeria's Armed Islamic Group seized an Air France Airbus at Algiers airport. French gendarmes stormed it in Marseille two days later.
alternates.significance: The hijackers were believed to have intended to crash the plane into Paris.
alternates.fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of December 27, 1994, carried Radio Algiers and Paris LCI Television on four men seizing an Air France Airbus in Algiers, a crisis team formed, and 19 passengers released.
